How to Digitize Small Business Processes Step by Step

Por Nube para Pymes / 01/08/2026

Are you still printing forms and transferring data by hand from a notebook to a spreadsheet? Digitizing small business processes does not require a technical team or a huge budget. Therefore, many business owners only begin this change when they have already lost time or money due to a manual transcription error.

Official source: Zapier official site.

  • Step 1: Identify the process that takes up the most time
  • Step 2: Choose a single tool for that process

Step 1: identify the process that takes up the most time

The first step to digitizing business processes is to identify which repetitive task takes up the most time each week. Therefore, write down how many times you do it and how long it takes each time. This way, you will know where to start without trying to change everything at once. Furthermore, this first process is usually the one that provides the most immediate benefit when digitized.

Step 2: Choose a single tool for that process

Don't try to digitize the entire business with a single giant platform from day one. Instead, choose a specific tool for the process you identified in the previous step. For example, if the problem is the agenda, just start there. Our guide on how to migrate from Excel to a CRM without losing data explains that first step when the process to digitize is customer registration.

Step 3: Train your team before demanding results

A tool change without training usually fails, no matter how good the chosen platform is. Also, give your team a week or two of practice before demanding that they abandon the previous method. In fact, many businesses make the mistake of requiring change overnight and end up with two systems running at once.

Step 4: Automate only what already works well manually

Automating a messy process only multiplies the mess at a faster rate. Therefore, it is advisable to organize the process by hand first, and only then add automation. Our guide on best AI tools to automate repetitive tasks helps you choose what to automate once the process is sorted.

What to look at besides the chosen tool

What to look at besides the tool matters as much as which platform you choose to digitize business processes. The team's resistance to change, for example, usually outweighs any technical function. Likewise, it is worth checking if your current data can be easily exported if you one day change tools.

What this looks like in practice

A small business gains order almost immediately just by digitizing one or two key processes. On the other hand, a business with more movement takes better advantage of automation once the team already masters the base tool. However, no software replaces the business owner's good judgment. In fact, it only orders the day-to-day operational part.

How to choose where to start based on your business

If your business is just starting, digitize customer registration and sales first. This way, you avoid losing valuable information from the beginning. On the other hand, if you have already been operating with paper processes for several years, it is advisable to start with the administrative process that consumes the most time each week. Likewise, our guide on how to save hours of administrative work with automation delves into that specific case.

Calculators and tools to start digitizing

Before automating a process, measure the cost of the problem and document the current flow. You can use free Cloud tools for SMEs as initial support:

  • On-Premise vs. Cloud Total Cost Simulator — compare infrastructure, maintenance and continuity costs.
  • Labor cost overrun calculator — estimate the effect of labor loads and costs before automating.
  • Free Cloud Tools for SMEs — browse the catalog and choose a small test.
What process should I digitize first?

Start with the process that is repetitive, measurable and with fewer exceptions: for example, requests, invoices, tracking or data consolidation.

Why measure before automating?

Because you need a baseline of time, errors, cost and people responsible to know if automation really improves the process.

Are calculators a substitute for a complete evaluation?

No. They serve to explore initial scenarios; Validate the assumptions and contrast the result with your real data before investing.

Frequently asked questions about digitizing business processes

Do I need to hire someone technical to get started? No, most of today's tools are designed to be configured without technical knowledge.

How long does it take to digitize the first process? It depends on the process. However, many businesses see results within two to three weeks of consistent use.

Can I digitize my entire business at once? It is not recommended. Since trying to change everything at once usually generates more resistance and errors in the team.

What happens if my team resists change? That is why it is advisable to train well before demanding results, and explain what specific problem the new tool solves.

How to Digitize Processes of a Small Business Step by Step: in summary

Digitizing small business processes works best when you start with a single process and train your team well before demanding results. First identify which task takes up the most time, choose a specific tool and only then add automation.
